problem:
Using the change of variables

$$
\displaystyle u = \frac{y}{x^{2}}, v = xy,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ in the first quadrant bounded by the curves
$$
\displaystyle y = x^{2}, y = 2x^{2}, y = \frac{1}{x}, y = \frac{4}{x}.
$$
worked_solution:
The given substitution turns the boundaries into $1\le u\le2$ and $1\le v\le4$. It is one-to-one in the first quadrant: $x=(v/u)^{1/3}$ and $y=u^{1/3}v^{2/3}$. The Jacobian is

$$
\frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)}=
\begin{vmatrix}-2y/x^3&1/x^2\\y&x\end{vmatrix}
=-\frac{3y}{x^2}=-3u.
$$

Area uses its absolute inverse, so

$$
\operatorname{Area}(D)=\int_1^2\int_1^4\frac1{3u}\,dv\,du=\ln2.
$$
